audit.whatIsWrong: The chart reads Ziggs/Ziggs/Ziggs/Skill/Ziggs/Skill/Ziggs — five of seven stages to Ziggs in a lane Singed wins 53.71% of. It also contradicts its own prose line by line: the page says 'Levels 4-6 are the pivot', that level 6 is when 'you close and run him down', and that 'post-Rylai's you win the side lane convincingly', yet the chart gives Ziggs level 6 and only calls first item even.
audit.why: Ziggs genuinely owns levels 1-3 — 850-range Bouncing Bomb on a 6s cooldown against a champion whose Q is a 20-unit aura. But the proxy at 4-5, Insanity Potion at 6 and Rylai's are all Singed stages, and at two items an artillery mage who contributes from safety is a genuine even call, not a win.
audit.corrected: Ziggs / Ziggs / Ziggs / Singed / Singed / Singed / Skill.

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one cooldown number appears in the matchup, and the full layer's difficulty rating is 8.5/10 while its verdict is FAV.
audit.why: The spikes here are all cooldown-shaped: Satchel Charge is his only escape and it is 20s at rank 1, Hexplosive Minefield never gets shorter than 16s at any rank, and Mega Inferno Bomb runs 120/95/70s. An 8.5/10 difficulty on a favoured 53.71% lane misprices the whole page.
audit.corrected: Ziggs spikes: levels 1-3 (Bouncing Bomb 6/5.5/5/4.5/4s at 850 range), Mega Inferno Bomb at 6 (120/95/70s, 5000 range). Singed spikes: 4-5 proxy, level 6 Insanity Potion, Rylai's. diffRating lowered from 8.5/10 to 7/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most useful interaction in this matchup is missing and one invented one is present. Missing: Hexplosive Minefield's own text says successive mine detonations on the same target deal reduced damage. The page instead treats the minefield as a wall that 'punishes any forced approach', which is the opposite conclusion. Invented: late says 'Respect his ult Mega Inferno Bomb for the slow zone'. Riot's description of Mega Inferno Bomb has no slow in it — enemies in the primary blast zone simply take more damage than those further out. Also unstated: Short Fuse's cooldown is reduced every time Ziggs casts an ability, so a Ziggs spamming Q gets his empowered auto back faster.
audit.why: The mine falloff is exactly the fact a Singed needs: running the whole field costs one full mine and then cheap repeats, which is why the run-through pattern works at all. Telling the player the field denies the approach talks them out of their own win condition. And a slow that does not exist changes how they path away from his ult.
audit.corrected: Hexplosive Minefield is a flat 16s at every rank, 900 range, and repeat detonations on the same target deal reduced damage — the first mine is the expensive one, so commit through rather than edging around. Satchel Charge (20/18/16/14/12s, 1000 range) knocks Ziggs away as well as you and is his only self-peel; once it is spent he has no escape. Mega Inferno Bomb is a damage zone with a hotter centre, not a slow. Short Fuse's cooldown drops every time he casts, so his empowered auto tracks his ability usage.

audit.whatIsWrong: Satchel Charge is named as the tracked cooldown in six places without ever being numbered.
audit.why: 20 seconds at rank 1 is the entire window the page is built around, and it only shrinks to 12 — that is worth stating because it stays a real window all game.
audit.corrected: Satchel Charge 20/18/16/14/12s. Bouncing Bomb 6/5.5/5/4.5/4s. Hexplosive Minefield a flat 16s. Mega Inferno Bomb 120/95/70s.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 are the pivot. The moment you have ghost and enough HP, start proxying behind his wave at his tower. Ziggs cannot stop Poison Trail from melting his own minions while he stands at the turret — he either stays and loses the wave or leaves to kill you, breaking his safe poke window. When he chases, ghost through his Minefield and run your pattern: he is not a melee brawler, and your Passive movement speed from running past him makes landing Bouncing Bomb mid-chase unreliable. At level 6 your Insanity Potion makes you suddenly bulky enough to absorb one Satchel Charge knockback and still close — bait the W first, then commit with ghost and Fling the moment the range opens.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 are the pivot. The moment you have ghost and enough HP, start proxying behind his wave at his tower. Ziggs cannot stop Poison Trail melting his own minions while he stands at the turret — he either stays and loses the wave or leaves to kill you, breaking his safe poke window. When he chases, ghost straight through the Minefield rather than around it: successive mine detonations on the same target deal reduced damage, so only the first one is expensive. Watch Short Fuse too — its cooldown drops every time he casts, so a Q-spamming Ziggs has the empowered auto up more often than you expect. At 6, bait Satchel Charge, then commit.

edits.before: Post-Rylai's you win the side lane convincingly. The slow on Poison Trail means Ziggs cannot simply walk out of your cloud — he has to Satchel Charge or he gets slowly dissolved, and you can track that cooldown. He out-ranges you into infinity in an open teamfight, so your win condition is not fighting him in the open field: it is threatening the tower, forcing him to teleport or miss objectives, and using Insanity Potion to 1v1 him in the side lane where his Bouncing Bomb arc is least reliable at close quarters. Respect his ult Mega Inferno Bomb for the slow zone — never stand still if his ult is off cooldown mid-chase.
edits.after: Post-Rylai's you win the side lane convincingly. The slow on Poison Trail means Ziggs cannot simply walk out of your cloud — he has to spend Satchel Charge, 12s even at rank 5, or he dissolves, and that cooldown is trackable. He out-ranges you into infinity in an open teamfight, so your win condition is not the open field: it is threatening the tower, forcing him to teleport or miss objectives, and using Insanity Potion to 1v1 him at close quarters. Mega Inferno Bomb is not a slow — it is a 5000-range damage zone with a hotter centre, so step off the middle rather than trying to outrun it, and never leave a chipped turret up for his Satchel to hexplode.

notes: All 3 suspectNames are false positives. IMPORTANT FLAG MISFIRE: ziggs.json tags Satchel Charge (W) with 'percentHealth', and champ-data/_kits/_missing/singed.json carries a derived line off it — 'Ziggs bypasses stacking resistances (Satchel Charge (W)) — raw armour or MR is the wrong answer here.' Riot's own description of Satchel Charge says only 'deals magic damage'; there is no max-health component in it. Per the trust-the-description rule I did not write that claim into the page, and the _missing entry for ziggs should be treated as unreliable. The other thing I could not resolve and left out: Mega Adhesive grounds, but Satchel Charge displaces Ziggs by knockback rather than by a dash, and I could not verify whether grounding prevents it — so I made no grounding claim in this matchup at all rather than guess. If someone can confirm it, that single line would be worth adding to wants.you.
